data.title: Poster session — row C
data.transcript: Speaker 1: Your poster on sensor drift is the one I wanted to find. I'm Tomasz Brekke, I review for the Journal of Field Instrumentation. Speaker 2: Oh, great, thanks for stopping. Speaker 1: Your calibration method looks solid, but the methods section skips how you handled the outliers. Speaker 2: Fair. I can send you the revised methods section with the outlier handling by Monday. Speaker 1: Please do. And we have a public drift dataset from the coastal buoys; I'll share the link with you this week. Speaker 2: That would help a lot. I should also read that 2019 paper on temperature compensation you mentioned. Speaker 1: Yes, Halvorsen and Ito. Here's my card.

data.title: After orbital mechanics class
data.transcript: Speaker 1: Did you finish problem set four? Speaker 2: Halfway. The Hohmann transfer part is killing me. Speaker 1: Want to work through it together Wednesday night in the library? Speaker 2: Yes, Wednesday at seven works. I'm Dan, by the way. Speaker 1: Amara. Also, did you see there's a registration hold on your account? Mine had one for the lab fee. Speaker 2: No, I didn't. I'll email Professor Lindqvist about it tomorrow so I can register for spring. Speaker 1: The set is due Friday at noon, don't forget.

data.title: Client kickoff — Harrowgate Freight
data.transcript: Speaker 1: Thanks for running the kickoff. I'm Celeste Varga, operations lead at Harrowgate Freight. Speaker 2: Glad to. So next step on our side is the onboarding checklist. I'll send it to you by Wednesday. Speaker 1: Good. Our finance team needs to know which fields map to their export. Speaker 2: I'll check with our data team and confirm the field mapping before the next call. Speaker 1: And can we book the training session for the week of the twentieth? Speaker 2: I'll send a calendar invite for training that week.

data.title: Career fair — booth 12
data.transcript: Speaker 1: Hi, I'm Rafael Okonjo, I recruit for mission operations at Kestrel Launch Systems. Speaker 2: Hi Rafael, I'm Dan. I've been looking at your flight controller trainee opening. Speaker 1: Great fit, from what you're describing. Send me your résumé and I'll pass it to the hiring manager. Speaker 2: I'll send it tonight. Speaker 1: And let's set up a screening call, maybe Thursday afternoon? Speaker 2: Thursday works. I'll reply to your scheduling email. Speaker 1: Also look at our engineering blog; the team posts about their console setup.

data.title: Coffee with an editor
data.transcript: Speaker 1: I'm Wren Castellanos, I edit the Lowlands Science Weekly newsletter. We'd love a piece from you on amateur ground stations. Speaker 2: I'd like that. I can get you a first draft by the end of the month. Speaker 1: Perfect, around twelve hundred words. Speaker 2: Understood. Speaker 1: And if you want a source, Oskar Lind built a station on his roof; he said he'd be happy to be interviewed. Speaker 2: Then I'll reach out to Oskar this week to set up the interview.

data.title: Astronomy club meeting
data.transcript: Speaker 1: Thanks for coming tonight. I'm Ingrid Solberg, I coordinate volunteers for the Northbank Astronomy Club. Speaker 2: Happy to be here. Speaker 1: We need someone to run a telescope at the public outreach night on the eighteenth. Speaker 2: Count me in, I'll take a telescope that night. Speaker 1: Wonderful. Also, early registration for the regional amateur astronomy conference closes Sunday. Speaker 2: Good to know, I'll register before then.

data.title: Call with my sister
data.transcript: Speaker 1: Don't forget Mom's birthday dinner is Saturday. Speaker 2: I know. I'll pick up the cake from Larkspur Bakery on Saturday morning. Speaker 1: And did you ever call your landlord about the leak under the sink? Speaker 2: Not yet. I'll call him tomorrow. Speaker 1: Also the library books are overdue. Speaker 2: Right, I'll drop them off this weekend.

data.title: Networking mixer
data.transcript: Speaker 1: Great talking with you. We should grab coffee sometime. Speaker 2: Definitely, let's stay in touch. Speaker 1: I'm Linnea, by the way. Speaker 2: Dan. Hey, do you know the name of the trio playing tonight? Their bass player is great. Speaker 1: No idea, sorry. Speaker 2: I'll look them up later.

data.title: Hallway at the symposium
data.transcript: Speaker 1: Dan, can I ask a favour? It's Mara Quist. Speaker 2: Of course. Speaker 1: Keep this between us, but I'm starting medical leave next week; my surgery got moved up. Could you give my talk on detector cooling in the Tuesday session? Speaker 2: I'm sorry, Mara. Yes, I'll present it for you. Speaker 1: Thank you. I'll send you the slides tonight. Speaker 2: I'll let the session chair know I'm presenting in your place, without the details.

data.title: Founder dinner
data.transcript: Speaker 1: Strictly confidential: we're in acquisition talks with a much bigger company, and the term sheet values us at forty million. Nobody outside the board knows. I'm Joaquim Reyes, by the way, founder of Brightwater Robotics. Speaker 2: Understood, that stays with me. Speaker 1: Do you know a good M and A lawyer? Speaker 2: I can introduce you to Hedda Nyquist, she handled a deal like this. I'll send the introduction tomorrow. Speaker 1: And send me the deck from your talk, too. Speaker 2: Will do.
